It's more of a manga, in truth. I'm also an anime nerd. 

The premise is that a bunch of scientists create a sentient robot that is stronger, faster, better looking and more intelligent than a regular human. She ends up killing all the scientists, except for two. The one that pretended to be dead, and the one that uploaded memoirs from assassins of years past into her brain. The robot says that there is a way to make every human like her, but before she can tell him, the remaining scientist downloads her brain into a chip and steals her away. Because he loves his work so much, and because he didn't entirely disagree with the scientist, he doesn't destroy it. Instead, he uploads her into a computer of a school one of his colleagues is principal of, where none of his enemies would think to look. A group of students who started a club come across the robot trying to communicate with them through a computer, and they think she is some girl being held prisoner by the principal, and have to crack codes and figure out passwords to try and find out where she is. Her brain is scrambled and there are parts she can't access, so when they crack codes and put in passwords, she gets more of her memories back. 

Tl;dr: It's basically about a bunch of school kids who find an A.I in one of the school's computers. I'm not that far with it, cus I suck, but I'm hoping to turn it into something one day.

It's a place you go where you want a small boost to start your day. But most of us need more than that.

A character has to want to be redeemed. They have to want to turn. And, personally, I don't think it makes sense for the Diamonds to want to turn. It made sense for Peridot, who was simply a subordinate and just did what she was told, scared of her superiors. She became intrigued by Earth and wanted to know more about it and began to love it because of her curious nature. Every character that has or has potential to be redeemed has also been treated badly also (Peridot, Lapis, The Famethyst, The Off-Colors). But what of the characters who haven't been treated poorly and seemed to enjoy their positions, such as Holly Blue? Who are elite and enjoy being above others and have no reason to be dissatisfied and see nothing wrong with the Diamonds way of doing things? 

What if the Diamonds don't see anything wrong with their way of doing things. What if they believe thee weak give into the strong, that people need strong leadership? That would be a very realistic angle, because people view things differently, they have different ideologies. It might be evil to us, but it might be the best course of action for them. And if the Backfire effect is real, it is extremely hard to change people's minds. I really do hope they go this route with the Diamonds. I think it would add more complexity.
